stage: Exploratory follow-up after native-control findings; no adopted research-question change
question: Does adding DEAP and GAMEEMO training data help SEED-IV binary recognition under otherwise matched trial-feature controls?
target: SEED-IV binary, same five predeclared 9/3/3 subject folds as the native-label diagnostic
sources: DEAP and GAMEEMO training participants only from the original seed-42 subject split; their validation/test participants are excluded from all fitting and selection
models: Joint training with one global training-fitted scaler
Joint training with separate training-fitted scalers for each dataset
common_features: Named common 14 electrodes; same four-band mean-window-log-power trial features; originals only; existing source-corrected cache
training: Class-balanced logistic regression; pooled models also give equal total weight to each dataset; same C candidates [0.01,0.1,1,10]
selection: SEED-IV validation trial balanced accuracy only; ties smallest C; no held-out thresholds or calibration
evaluation: Previously inspected SEED-IV development folds; same test trials in every comparison; 0.5 decision threshold
purpose: Diagnose potential benefit or negative transfer from pooling before selecting a paper contribution
limitations: Classical trial features do not establish behavior of neural architectures. Source-specific scaling uses available training participants from all three known datasets, not zero-shot transfer. Source weights and training sample count are declared; semantics, acquisition differences and dataset size cannot be disentangled from the pooling comparison alone.
